name: Seattle Public Schools
text: No police on campus since 2020. In October 2025 the board voted 5–2 against a one-year "School Engagement Officer" pilot at Garfield High. Superintendent Ben Shuldiner, who started in February 2026, has said he favors unarmed district safety officers, and in October 2026 the board backed pilots of walk-through weapons detectors at Rainier Beach and Nathan Hale high schools. Security staff are district employees under Policy 4311.

name: Renton School District
text: Since 2025-26, a Renton Police school resource officer works full time at each comprehensive high school (Renton, Hazen, Lindbergh).

name: Kent School District
text: Contracts with Kent Police for two school resource officers and a commander who serves as safety liaison, alongside district Safety Services staff.

name: Bellevue School District
text: Removed campus officers in 2021. Since fall 2022, sworn Bellevue Police "Community Engagement Officers" work from the central office and cover groups of schools.

name: Issaquah School District
text: Doesn't use school resource officers. A district Safety and Security Department runs safety under Regulation 4312, including threat assessment.

name: Tahoma School District (Maple Valley)
text: Maple Valley and Covington contract with the King County Sheriff's Office for policing, and the Sheriff's Southeast Precinct in Maple Valley provides school resource officers to the district. In the 2021-22 and 2023-24 federal data, Tahoma High reported about one full-time sworn officer and each middle school about three-quarters of one; no elementary school reported one.

name: Every Washington district
text: Must have a bullying (HIB) policy with a compliance officer (RCW 28A.600.477), a behavioral threat-assessment program (RCW 28A.320.123), discipline rules that limit exclusion (WAC 392-400), and a weapons ban on school grounds (RCW 9.41.280).
